title: Boston Dynamics' New 4-Finger Hand Is Built for Hyundai's Robot Mass Production
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 2, 2026

Boston Dynamics unveiled a next-generation 4-finger robot hand with 13 degrees of freedom, built to operate real industrial tools and ready for mass production at Hyundai Motor Group's new U.S. robotics plant. Here's what was disclosed about the hand and Hyundai's manufacturing buildout around it.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Hyundai Motor Group
KRX: 005380 (Hyundai Motor)		Owner of Boston Dynamics; building the robot's mass-production plant and deploying it across its own factoriesReported: company robotics announcement, Oct 2, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • Hardware upgrade: The new hand has 13 degrees of freedom, up from the prior model's 7 — one 4-DOF opposable thumb plus three 3-DOF fingers, roughly the size of an adult hand, with a grip strength over 45kg (100+ lbs).
  • Sensing: High-density tactile pressure sensors are built into the fingertips and palm for fine force control during manipulation tasks.
  • Deliberately 3-fingered-plus-thumb, not 5-fingered: Boston Dynamics' Chief Product Technology Officer Zack Jackowski said the company dropped the pinky after testing: developers taped their pinky and ring fingers together for a full workday and found the pinky "is not essential for work tasks." The company prioritized manufacturing reliability over fully mimicking human anatomy.
  • Tool use: The hand is built to operate electric drills, torque drivers, grinders, nail guns, and welding torches — real industrial tools, not just pick-and-place objects.
  • Design for mass production: Actuators are sealed and modular internally, removing external cabling as a failure point. The hand was designed from the start around simulation-based reinforcement learning ("Sim2Real") and domain-randomization training.
  • Hyundai's buildout: Hyundai Motor Group is setting up a "Robot Metaplant Application Center" (RMAC) at its Georgia, U.S. facility, with a target of 30,000 robots/year of U.S. production capacity by 2028, and plans to roll out 25,000 Atlas units across Hyundai-Kia's global manufacturing plants over time.

Why this matters for Korean supply chains

Boston Dynamics has been a Hyundai Motor Group subsidiary since 2021, so this hand's path to mass production runs directly through Hyundai's own manufacturing network rather than a third party. As Hyundai scales humanoid and Atlas production domestically in the U.S., component sourcing — actuators, tactile sensors, precision gearing — becomes a sourcing opportunity its existing Korean supply base (auto-parts and electronics affiliates) is positioned to compete for, though no specific component suppliers for this hand were named in current reporting. (Reported)

What's still unconfirmed

No manufacturer was named for the hand's actuators, sensors, or other components. Pricing, the production timeline for the hand itself (as distinct from the broader Atlas rollout), and which Hyundai-Kia plants will receive the first units were not disclosed. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Why does the hand have 4 fingers instead of 5?
Boston Dynamics found through internal testing that the pinky finger wasn't essential for the work tasks the hand needs to perform, and dropping it simplifies manufacturing and improves reliability.

Is this hand already in production?
Not confirmed. Hyundai is building the manufacturing capacity (targeting 30,000 robots/year by 2028 at its Georgia plant), but no production start date specific to this hand was given.

Does this relate to Hyundai's other robot plans?
Yes. This hand is meant for Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid, which Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 units of across its Hyundai-Kia manufacturing plants globally.
